title: Release and rollback
outcome: Explain release and rollback using the deciding step in this fictional service.
scenario: A higher score can still block release. Version B is proposed to replace A; every privacy gate is mandatory.
given: A passes 8/10 correctness cases. B passes 9/10 but fails one mandatory privacy check.

steps.label: Compute quality
steps.detail: Correctness rises from 80% to 90% on these cases.

steps.label: Apply privacy gate
steps.detail: The mandatory failure blocks B’s release.

steps.label: Keep recovery ready
steps.detail: Retain the reviewed A version and documented rollback procedure.

explanation: Release criteria combine benefits and mandatory conditions. Rollback requires known versions and compatible data, not an informal promise.

counterfactual.change: Repair B and pass privacy on a fresh reserved case.
counterfactual.prediction: B may enter the remaining gates; one repair does not approve everything.
counterfactual.reason: All required release conditions still apply.

student_task: Compute A’s and B’s correctness percentages. Why is B still blocked, and does passing a fresh privacy check automatically satisfy every release gate?
teacher_answer: Correctness rises from 80% to 90% on these cases. The mandatory failure blocks B’s release. Retain the reviewed A version and documented rollback procedure. Changed case: B may enter the remaining gates; one repair does not approve everything. All required release conditions still apply.
project_evidence: For the Grounded Learning Service, retain an annotated trace and the changed-case result. Name the contract or evidence that makes the deciding step valid, so another team can review it.
limits: Rolling back code may not reverse earlier external effects or incompatible data changes.
review_note: Individually authored fictional practice, distinct from the reserved independent case. These stipulated records illustrate reasoning; no real service execution or learner outcome is claimed.
